_about: Independent ratings (4 Nov 2026) of the 16 competitor ad screenshots the founder shared (GIVA 10, Palmonas 2, Snitch 1, Lenskart 3), out of 10, with what Naira should take and avoid.

ads.product: Two rose-gold-tone 925 silver bracelets worn stacked: an infinity-link CZ pavé bracelet and a square-link bracelet with pink baguette stones and a clover charm
ads.format: 9:16 static, full-bleed on-model lifestyle photo (Story/Reels placement, seen in Meta Ad Library)
ads.hook_text: GIVA / Stack it up / Turn the charm up / FLAT 15% OFF / on purchase of ₹999 / CODE: NEW15 / SHOP NOW / *T&C Apply
ads.offer: Flat 15% off on ₹999+, code NEW15 (caption adds 925 silver, free shipping, easy returns)
ads.cta: SHOP NOW on a white pill inside the offer badge, plus Meta's Shop Now button
ads.visual_device: Warm editorial close-up: a hand resting on the wrist so the two bracelets catch the light against skin, a cream robe and a beige ground. The brown offer sticker is the highest-contrast thing on the canvas.
ads.why_score: The photo is pretty and believable, but it is beige on beige and looks like every jewellery ad in the feed. The bracelets sit small in the middle third, and the brown discount badge pulls the eye away from them. 'Stack it up / Turn the charm up' is a rhyme that could sell any bracelet, and the code adds friction. It is competent template work that fits the brand but has no idea that would stop a thumb.
ads.steal: Take the stack idea, because it maps straight onto Naira's real multi-buy. Put three wrist crops from the worn pool side by side as one stack: kiss-knot-bangle-worn, silk-mesh-cuff-worn and prism-riviere-bracelet-worn are the same model, mustard slip and warm light, so they read as one person's wrist. Give each its price. The offer goes low as the twist: 'Buy 3, get 20% off. Applied in your bag.' Also take the tight skin-and-light crop at the wrist, since Naira's worn photos already have this warmth.
ads.avoid: Do not composite several pieces onto one wrist, because that changes the photo. Avoid a generic rhyme line, a chunky sticker badge with a code sitting on the product photo, small T&C text, and letting the jewellery shrink to the middle third.

ads.product: Rose-gold-tone 925 silver openwork double-loop bracelet with CZ dots, standing against a maroon GIVA gift box
ads.format: 9:16 static, flat blush ground with a packshot and a graphic paper prop (content packed into the top 55%)
ads.hook_text: GIVA / Gift receipt? / SHE'S KEEPING IT. / [receipt:] GIVA / ORDER SUMMARY / Bracelet ×1 / Gift-ready box  Yes / Her reaction  Priceless / Code BLING  -20% / on orders above ₹999 / TOTAL  Worth it / SHOP NOW / *T&C apply
ads.offer: Flat 20% off on orders above ₹999, code BLING, written as a line item inside the receipt
ads.cta: SHOP NOW maroon button, plus Meta's Shop Now button
ads.visual_device: A mock 'order summary' receipt with a zigzag tear and joke line items, paired with an italic-serif question and a bold caps answer ('Gift receipt? / SHE'S KEEPING IT.')
ads.why_score: The receipt prop interrupts the pattern, and the headline answers the gifting worry ('will she return it?') with a smile. Putting the 20% inside the joke is smarter than shouting it. But the bracelet is a small flat packshot, rose gold on blush is low contrast, and 'Priceless' is a borrowed cliché. Almost half the 9:16 canvas is empty blush, which wastes the Story.
ads.steal: Deliver the offer inside a joke object as line items, not as a badge, and use the two-tier 'question? / Answer.' headline. Port it to an object Naira is allowed to use: a handwritten paper note or a potli gift tag in Kalam/Caveat. List three pool pieces with exact prices, then a closing line of facts, e.g. 'Gift box: every time. 3 pieces: 20% off, applied in your bag.' The gift-box line is a true Naira fact ('Every piece arrives in the Naira gift box').
ads.avoid: Avoid a receipt or order-summary look, because Naira's brief bans imitating a real document. Also avoid the 'Priceless' cliché, an all-caps sentence (Naira allows only one short caps word), and leaving the lower 40% of a Story empty.

ads.product: Rose-gold-tone adjustable cluster ring with blue, light-blue and lilac CZ flowers
ads.format: 9:16 static, packshot in an arched cut-out window on a beige ground, with a maroon offer footer
ads.hook_text: GIVA / Her "yes" / STILL SPARKLES. / Celebrate every year of it. / Certified Jewellery. Anti-Microbial. Hypo-allergenic. / *T&C apply / Flat 20% OFF above ₹999 / Code: BLING | SHOP NOW
ads.cta: SHOP NOW in the footer bar, plus Meta's Shop Now button
ads.visual_device: An arch-shaped window framing the ring on white, with the blue stones as the only saturated colour, then the italic-serif lead plus heavy caps payoff
ads.why_score: The arch frame is tidy and the blue stones give one colour pop, so the ring looks good. But the 'her yes' anniversary line on a non-solitaire floral cluster ring is a mixed signal (is it an engagement ring?). The claims row and the full-width maroon offer band fill about a third of the frame. It reads as a template rather than an idea.
ads.steal: Use the arch window as a repeatable frame for a whole-collection grid. Make 4 or 6 identical arches, each holding a tight crop of a different pool hero (H02 Prism Rivière ₹2,399, H08 Woven Gold Hoops ₹1,199, H15 Bold Nocturne Chain ₹1,799, H11 Emerald tennis ₹1,499, H04 Prism Cluster Studs ₹1,499, H10 Toggle Link Chain ₹1,199) with the price under each. One shape repeated says 'a collection', and each piece still gets its own ground. Also take the italic-serif lead plus a short bold payoff (CGI italic + Velista in the kit).
ads.avoid: Avoid the claims line: 'hypo-allergenic' is banned for Naira, and certification claims are not available. Avoid a heavy offer band across the bottom, a romantic-partner line that shuts out the woman buying for herself, and caps sentences.

ads.product: Rose-gold-tone antler (deer) pendant necklace with a heart-cut CZ, on a purple velvet bust
ads.format: 9:16 static sale creative, monochrome aubergine studio set with icon trust badges and a bottom offer strip
ads.hook_text: GIVA / PRICE DROP ON / GIVA bestsellers / Certified jewellery / Hypoallergenic / Anti-microbial / Price Drop | Upto 50% OFF | SHOP NOW
ads.offer: 'Price drop' on bestsellers, up to 50% off (caption: bestselling 925 silver, quality, hypoallergenic, anti-microbial)
ads.cta: SHOP NOW in the white bottom strip, plus Meta's Shop Now button
ads.visual_device: A saturated aubergine monochrome ground and velvet bust, with the sparkly heart as the single bright point and three stacked icon badges
ads.why_score: The deep purple stands out among beige feeds, and the heart CZ catches light. But 'up to 50%' is vague and reads as a markdown on an inflated price. The icon badges look like pharmacy packaging, and a whimsical deer pendant is an odd face for 'bestsellers'. The offer strip sits where the Story reply bar would cover it.
ads.steal: Use a 'bestsellers' umbrella to sell a collection, in Naira's honest version: 'Our most-clicked pieces' (true per pool proof) or the site's 'Most loved' trio (Prism Rivière ₹2,399, Woven Gold Hoops ₹1,199, Bold Nocturne Chain ₹1,799) as a three-card Shop All opener. Also take the monochrome ground matched to the piece, which H15 (Nocturne chain on the maroon-and-gold saree) already does inside the pool.
ads.avoid: Avoid 'Price drop / Upto 50% OFF', since percent-off against compare-at prices is banned for Naira, and avoid hypoallergenic or anti-microbial badges (banned). No icon badge stacks. Never put copy or the offer below y=1500 on a Story.

ads.product: Four gold-tone (gold-plated 925 silver) CZ rings: split-shank solitaire, slim solitaire, pavé disc and an open-bar solitaire band
ads.format: 9:16 static range shot on a raked maroon CGI-style pedestal (shown in the Meta Ad Library list view)
ads.hook_text: GIVA / Silver rings you'll wear on repeat / FLAT 15% OFF / on purchase of ₹999 / CODE : NEW15 / *T&C Apply
ads.offer: Flat 15% off on ₹999+, code NEW15. The caption lists: Get Flat 15% OFF using code NEW15 / Free Shipping / Easy Returns. The headline reads 'Grab Style sealed in Silver'.
ads.cta: Meta Shop Now button (no on-image button)
ads.visual_device: A lineup of four rings standing in a row on one lit surface, so the range shows at a glance
ads.why_score: This is the only GIVA ad in the batch that shows range, which matters for Shop All. But at feed size the rings fill about 20% of the frame on a dark maroon field and vanish. The words say 'silver rings' while the rings look gold, which is a confusing mismatch. 'Wear on repeat' is a line that could sell anything, and the offer box is the same NEW15 template again.
ads.steal: Take the lineup: several pieces in one row on one ground tells 'a whole collection' in a second. Naira can build it from pool cut-outs (H10 toggle chain, H08 hoops, H16 knot bangle, H13 halo ring crop) laid in a row on cream paper with prices in Indian commas, and a line that names the count truthfully ('130+ pieces, from ₹599'). Also take the caption's line-item benefits as plain sentences: 'Free insured shipping. 3-5 working days. 7-day returns. Cash on delivery.'
ads.avoid: Avoid letting product scale fall under a third of the frame, a glossy CGI pedestal that cheapens real photos, copy that names a metal the picture contradicts (Naira must say gold tone or silver tone exactly), and the generic 'on repeat' line.

ads.product: Same creative as ea6ce15f, zoomed in: four gold-tone (gold-plated 925 silver) CZ rings on a maroon pedestal
ads.format: 9:16 static range shot (zoomed screenshot of the same Ad Library card)
ads.hook_text: [GIVA, cropped] / Silver rings you ' ll wear on repeat / FLAT 15% OFF / on purchase of ₹999 / CODE : NEW15
ads.cta: None on the image; Meta Shop Now button
ads.visual_device: Four rings in a row, with stones catching studio highlights against diagonal maroon light planes
ads.why_score: This is the same ad, so the scores match, but the zoom shows two things. First, the rings look much better big, so desire rises when the product fills the frame. Second, the headline's apostrophe renders as a broken glyph ('you ' ll'), a craft slip that cheapens a jewellery brand at phone size.
ads.steal: Crop tight. In a multi-piece Shop All grid, crop each piece to fill its cell rather than shrinking whole scenes, because the pieces sell when they are big. Also run a glyph check on every render: apostrophes, ₹ and Indian commas in Velista/Jost/CG at 26 px or more, looked at by eye.
ads.avoid: Avoid broken or fallback glyphs, rings at thumbnail scale, and the logo half-cropped at the top edge.

ads.product: Three rose-gold-tone 925 silver stacking rings (square halo, marquise wave band, solitaire with a leaf band) worn across three fingers
ads.format: 9:16 static lifestyle photo with a red headline band and an offer box
ads.hook_text: GIVA / Less price / Same silver sparkle / FLAT 15% OFF / on purchase of ₹999 / CODE : NEW15 / SHOP NOW / *T&C Apply
ads.offer: Flat 15% off on ₹999+, code NEW15 (caption: '...worth celebrating. GIVA Silver... the pocket')
ads.cta: SHOP NOW white button, plus Meta's Shop Now button
ads.visual_device: An unexpected context: a manicured hand on a maroon car's chrome wing mirror, with a reflection, and three rings stacked across the fingers
ads.why_score: The car mirror is the one genuinely fresh setting in the batch: chrome and a hand read as 'on my way out' and feel aspirational. Three rings on one hand suggests buying more than one. But 'Less price / Same silver sparkle' is clunky and leads with cheapness. The red band and offer box sit on top of the photo, and the lower third is dead maroon.
ads.steal: Take the everyday-but-specific context for a hand. Naira already has four in the pool: H03 wrist on a teak threshold, H13 hand of cards on green baize, H14 hand tying a mango-leaf toran, H07 hoops in an open palm. Make them one Shop All carousel or grid of hands in mid-plan, each with a concrete named moment and the piece's price, closing on the collection. Also take the visual of several pieces worn at once as a quiet cue for 'Buy 3, get 20% off'.
ads.avoid: Avoid a discount-led headline ('Less price'), which makes the pieces feel cheap. Avoid a solid colour band laid across the photo and a lower third with nothing in it.

ads.product: Rose-gold-tone adjustable blue CZ floral cluster ring (same ring as bb7cb273) in an arch window
ads.format: 9:16 static with a graphic checklist card and a packshot on a beige ground
ads.hook_text: GIVA / Your Diwali gifting list? / SORTED IN ONE CART. / Gifting list / ☑ Wife / ☑ Mom / ☑ Sister / ☑ Bestie / ☑ Me (obviously) [each name struck through] / FLAT 20% OFF on orders above ₹999 / Code: BLING | SHOP NOW / *T&C apply
ads.offer: Flat 20% off on orders above ₹999, code BLING (caption: '...sisters gets something... for yourself too')
ads.cta: SHOP NOW white button beside a black 'Code: BLING' block, plus Meta's Shop Now button
ads.visual_device: A checklist card whose struck-through names build a rhythm that lands on the punchline 'Me (obviously)', the self-gifting twist
ads.why_score: This is the best of the batch and the closest to a Shop All idea: one cart for everyone is a collection-level message, and the list is native and readable at phone size. 'Me (obviously)' is the line that earns the smile. But it shows one ring for a five-person list, which undercuts the promise. 'Wife' at the top frames the buyer as a husband, and the 20% and code take a big slab.
ads.steal: Use the list as a Shop All device in Naira's voice and handwriting (Kalam/Caveat on paper). Write the women she buys for, each struck off with a different pool piece and its exact price, e.g. 'Mummy, Bold Nocturne Chain ₹1,799 / Didi, Woven Gold Hoops ₹1,199 / Bhabhi, Kiss Knot Bangle ₹1,199 / Me, Prism Rivière ₹2,399', each name paired with a small crop of that piece. The list's length is the multi-buy, so the twist line can be 'Three or more: 20% off, applied in your bag.' Keep the self-gift as the last beat, in Naira's own words, not GIVA's.
ads.avoid: Avoid one product standing in for a list of many, a list headed by 'Wife' (Naira's buyer is a woman shopping for herself and her women), a code to type, an all-caps headline, and copying 'Me (obviously)' word for word.

ads.product: Silver wavy bracelet set with a line of small white stones, adjustable chain extender
ads.format: 9:16 static, split-screen diptych: worn on a wrist (left) against the packshot on ivory satin (right)
ads.hook_text: GIVA | FLAT 15%OFF on your first purchase | Code: NEW15
ads.offer: Flat 15% off the first purchase with code NEW15, on the image and repeated in the headline
ads.cta: No CTA on the image; Meta 'Shop now' button
ads.visual_device: A hairline split: the dark worn panel against the light satin packshot, with the wave shape repeating across both halves
ads.why_score: Clean and honest, and the diptych answers 'how big is it'. But silver-tone on grey and ivory has no colour to pop, the bottom third is empty satin, and the offer is the standard first-order code the whole category runs. Nothing makes a thumb stop.
ads.steal: Steal the 'on her | laid down' diptych with a hairline divider. For Shop All, stack four of them as rows in a Story, worn crop left and hero scene right: Prism Rivière (worn/prism-riviere-bracelet-worn.jpg | H02), Woven Gold Hoops (worn | H08), Bold Nocturne Chain (worn | H15) and Toggle Link Chain (worn | H10). 'Most loved' and 'our most-clicked pieces' are both true for these, and the pairing shows scale for every piece at once. Also take the quiet offer lockup: a thin rule with a small kicker, 'Buy 3 · 20% off · applied in your bag', bottom right at 30 px, never the headline.
ads.avoid: Codes and 'first purchase' (the brief bans codes). A lone silver-tone piece on grey with no colour contrast. A dead bottom third. The logo floating mid-frame.

ads.product: Rose-gold-tone open-link bracelet beside a maroon GIVA gift box (anniversary gifting)
ads.format: 9:16 static styled as a text-message conversation (platform-native or lo-fi)
ads.hook_text: GIVA | Anniversary is in 3 days. Help. | Something she'll wear every day. | [bracelet + GIVA box photo] | Ordered. You're a lifesaver. | When in doubt, GIFT GIVA. | Flat 20% off on min. purchase ₹999 | Code: BLING | Shop Now | *T&C apply
ads.offer: Flat 20% off on a minimum purchase of ₹999 with code BLING (T&C apply), on the image and in the primary text
ads.cta: On-image 'Shop Now' pill plus the Meta button
ads.visual_device: Maroon and white chat bubbles that read like a DM: problem, answer, relief in three lines
ads.why_score: The best idea in GIVA's pair: a native format with a mini story and a real buying moment. It is let down by execution. The chat block sits in the middle half of a mostly empty frame, the bubble type is about 20 px at phone size, the product is a postage stamp, and 'Something she'll wear every day' could sell any brand.
ads.steal: Steal the three-bubble story with the offer as the punchline, in plain Naira bubbles: no app chrome, names, avatars, ticks or timestamps, so it reads as a dramatization, not a fake screenshot. For example: 'Didi, Mummy and me. One order.' / '130+ pieces from ₹599. Buy 3, 20% off, applied in the bag.' / 'Three gift boxes. Sorted.' Swap GIVA's single thumbnail for a 3-up strip of worn photos (woven hoops, nocturne chain, verdant band) so the answer is literally the collection. Fill the frame: bubbles at 34 px or more, and on Story the chat runs the whole y=270-1500 band.
ads.avoid: Tiny type in a half-empty canvas. One product shown thumbnail-size. A brand-name pun in caps ('GIFT GIVA.'). Code and T&C clutter. Generic lines that fit any jeweller. Anything that looks like WhatsApp or a real app's UI.

ads.product: Gift combo: gold-tone emerald-green octagon pendant on a bead-station chain, matching emerald huggie hoops, and a star-printed Palmonas gift box
ads.format: 9:16 static still life with an offer lockup
ads.hook_text: Gifted in PALMONAS | Gifts that feel personal | Gift combos at 50% OFF | SHOP NOW
ads.offer: Gift combos at 50% off, on the image and in the headline ('...OFF on PALMONAS Gift Combos'); reads as a markdown against compare-at prices
ads.cta: On-image outlined 'SHOP NOW' box plus the Meta button
ads.visual_device: A chocolate-brown ground with one raking diagonal light, emerald green against brown, and the big white printed box as the anchor shape
ads.why_score: The richest frame in the batch. The dark warm ground makes gold-tone and green sing, and the set reads instantly as a ready gift. What holds it down: the biggest type is '50% OFF', a saturated and inflated hook; 'Gifts that feel personal' says nothing; and the bottom fifth is empty brown.
ads.steal: Steal the deep single-colour ground with one raking light, and a small set grouped around one anchor. Naira already has this look in H15 (Bold Nocturne Chain on the maroon-and-gold saree) and H13 (card night, dark bokeh): open a Shop All with a dark frame so it breaks a cream-heavy feed. The combo logic fits the real offer: show three pieces from three categories (chain, hoops, ring) and let 'Buy 3, 20% off' be shown, not shouted.
ads.avoid: A percentage off as the largest type, and any markdown against compare-at prices (both banned for Naira). Lines that fit any brand. Leaving the bottom fifth empty.

ads.product: Gift combo: gold-tone flower-station necklace and puffed-heart charm huggie hoops laid on the star-printed Palmonas gift box
ads.format: 9:16 static still life, headline at the top
ads.hook_text: Gifted in PALMONAS | Gift combos at 50% OFF | SHOP NOW
ads.offer: Gift combos at 50% off (same campaign as the brown ad)
ads.cta: On-image outlined 'SHOP NOW' box plus the Meta button
ads.visual_device: An ivory grosgrain ribbon looping across blush sand, with the jewellery laid on the gift box lid
ads.why_score: Clear and tidy, and parking the text at the top keeps it off the product. But blush on white on gold has no dark value, so it vanishes at thumbnail size. The jewellery is small, and you read four lines of offer before you reach a product. It looks like every gifting ad.
ads.steal: Steal the jewellery placed on its packaging, so 'gift' reads without a word, and the ribbon curve as a leading line into the piece. Keep text on clean ground above the product. Pool equivalent: H09 (four huggie pairs in front of four satin potlis), cropped tighter so the jewellery is bigger (ruby has only 4 units, so favour the crystal, emerald and amethyst pairs), with 'Every piece arrives in the Naira gift box.' as a small fact line.
ads.avoid: Pastel on pastel with nothing dark in the frame. Jewellery under about 15% of the area. Stacking the offer as the first thing read.

ads.product: Men's tan suede cross-strap slide sandals with cork footbed (new arrivals)
ads.format: About 1:1 static, a type-led product and price poster
ads.offer: No discount: an honest price as the hook (headline 'Are Here. Starting ₹1599.')
ads.cta: No CTA on the image; Meta 'Shop now' button (Tamil locale)
ads.visual_device: Giant condensed type in the sandal's own tan, with the product overlapping the headline for depth, a pun on the product's verb ('stepped'), and a huge price numeral
ads.why_score: The best-built ad in the batch: one colour family, instant read, the price as the reason, and a pun that belongs to the product. For its own male audience it is about 7.2. Scored for urban women, a men's sandal mostly scrolls past, and the three-line caps shout is loud.
ads.steal: Steal the tonal type with a cut-out breaking the headline, and the honest price as the giant hero numeral. Shop All version: 'from ₹599' huge in --gold #9A6B2F on cream, with a row of 5-6 cut-outs overlapping the top of the numerals and '130+ pieces' small above. Use solid shapes that cut cleanly: mesh cuff H05, kiss knot bangle H16, emerald tennis H11, crystal tennis H12, woven hoops H08. A price floor is the one number nobody in jewellery is shouting; they all shout percentages. Also borrow the verb pun as Naira's 'X, not Y' craft line.
ads.avoid: Three lines of ALL CAPS (the brief allows one short caps word). '₹1599' without the Indian comma. A single ₹1,799 piece beside a giant '₹599', which reads as that piece's price and misleads; show a spread so 'from' is true at a glance. 'Just in' newness claims.

ads.product: Black acetate square optical frame with clear temples
ads.format: 4:5 static studio product hero (one card of a series)
ads.offer: None on the image; the primary text carries a '₹...0 off. Use Code: SINGLE' deal
ads.cta: No CTA on the image; Meta button (Hindi locale)
ads.visual_device: The product levitating diagonally on a cool blue-grey spotlight gradient, filling about 70% of the frame
ads.why_score: A premium-looking object shot, but cold. 'Own Your Look' could sell anything, and there is no price, offer or reason on the image, so all the persuasion is buried in the caption.
ads.steal: Steal the series template: one piece, huge, centred on a spotlight gradient, with the type in the same position on every card. As a Shop All carousel: 8-10 cards, each a clean cut-out on a ground sampled from its own stone or metal (emerald bracelet H11 on bottle green, crystal H12 on cool grey, mesh cuff H05 on amber). Put the piece name and exact price in the same corner each time. The consistent frame says 'a collection', and the colour shift keeps the swipe going.
ads.avoid: Two-word slogans with nothing specific in them (Naira's generic lines stayed under 2.2%). No price on the image. A CGI-levitation look that makes jewellery read as a render and costs trust.

ads.product: Black acetate rectangular optical frame with textured metal temple cores
ads.format: 4:5 static studio product hero (same series as 'Own Your Look')
ads.offer: None on the image; the caption carries the '...0 off. Use Code: SINGLE' deal
ads.cta: No CTA on the image; Meta button (Hindi locale)
ads.visual_device: A black object against an amber-to-black radial glow, floating on a diagonal
ads.why_score: The warm glow behind a black object is the highest-contrast frame here, and it beats the blue version. But 'Crafted Boldly' is an empty claim, and the image gives no price or proof.
ads.steal: Use the amber-to-black radial behind gold-tone pieces as the opener card of a Shop All carousel. H07 (woven hoops in a palm on dark warm bokeh) already has this, so the first frame stops before the cream cards follow. If you claim craft, make it specific and true ('Woven, not cast.' ran 5.81%).
ads.avoid: Vague craft adjectives like 'Crafted Boldly'. An image that carries no reason to tap.

ads.product: Vincent Chase Sleek Steel thin metal rectangular frame with blue temples
ads.format: 1:1 static: UGC-style selfie with a product 'ticket' card overlaid in the lower third
ads.offer: None on the image; '₹800 off.' in the primary text
ads.cta: No CTA on the image; Meta 'Shop now' button
ads.visual_device: A close-up face with eye contact and phone-selfie realism, plus a notched white card holding the packshot and naming the exact model
ads.why_score: Face plus eye contact stops well, and worn-plus-packshot-plus-name is clear. But the model is an off-target man for urban Indian women, the white card eats 30% of the frame, and there is no price on the image.
ads.steal: Steal the worn photo with a product 'ticket' that names the exact piece. Naira's Bestsellers carousel (5.45% CTR, 33 purchases) was built on the worn listing photos; for Shop All, add a small cream ticket to the bottom of each card with the piece close-up (worn/<handle>-close.jpg) and 'Woven Gold Hoops · ₹1,199'. Each card becomes a mini product page without covering her face or the piece.
ads.avoid: Selfie 'UGC' realism Naira can't honestly make: no new photos, and presenting listing photos as customer selfies would be fake UGC. A heavy white card covering a third of the photo. An off-target model.

patterns: Batch 1 is all GIVA, and ea6ce15f and ec1cffb4 are the same creative. It is one template system: GIVA wordmark at the top, a two-tier headline (italic-serif question, then a bold sans-caps answer: 'Gift receipt? / SHE'S KEEPING IT.', 'Her "yes" / STILL SPARKLES.', 'Your Diwali gifting list? / SORTED IN ONE CART.'), a packshot or hand, then a code-based offer block. The question-and-answer headline is their house hook, and it is the most transferable piece; Naira's version would be CGI italic plus Velista, without the caps sentence.

Every ad carries a percent-off code (NEW15 for 15% on ₹999, BLING for 20% on ₹999+, 'Upto 50%' price drop). The offer often has the largest type and takes 15-30% of the canvas. The feed is saturated with codes, so Naira's genuine edge is putting the multi-buy low as the twist and saying 'applied in your bag'. There is no code to type, and that frictionlessness is a selling point.

The two strongest ads (the receipt and the gifting checklist) both use a paper prop as graphic: a printed object with line items that delivers a joke and folds the offer inside it. Naira can't use a receipt (it imitates a real document), but a handwritten list, note or potli gift tag gives the same mechanic legally and in brand voice.

No ad actually sells a collection. Most show one SKU, and the two range shots (4 rings on a pedestal, 3 rings on a hand) shrink the product to about 20% of the frame. 'Show many pieces, each big, each priced' is open white space for a Naira Shop All. Repeat one frame shape (an arch, a cell, a card) so many pieces read as one system.

Gifting framing dominates (gift receipt, gifting list, anniversary 'yes'), and the buyer is often coded as a man ('Wife' first, 'Her yes'). Naira's buyer is a woman shopping for herself and the women around her. The line that lands in the batch is the self-gift ('Me (obviously)'), so Naira should build lists and lines around her and her women (Mummy, Didi, Bhabhi, herself).

The lines are generic and could sell anything: 'Stack it up / Turn the charm up', 'Silver rings you'll wear on repeat', 'Less price / Same silver sparkle'. None names a concrete Indian thing. This is exactly the class of line Naira's data shows stays under 2.2%, and it is Naira's clearest differentiator (anaar, rangoli, pheni, toran, saree).

GIVA's trust layer is claims (certified, hypoallergenic, anti-microbial, 925 silver) that Naira is barred from. Naira's truthful equivalents are service facts: free insured shipping, 3-5 working days, 7-day returns, cash on delivery, and every piece in the Naira gift box. These belong in the caption or a small line, not as icon badges.

The palettes are warm-muted: blush, beige, maroon, aubergine, with rose-gold-tone metal on similar tones. Low contrast is the default, so Naira's pastel rangoli/candy heroes (H01, H02, H04) and the ruby-on-blush anaar (H06) would read louder in this feed without shouting.

Lifestyle hands beat flat packshots for desire: the bracelet stack and the car-mirror rings score highest on desire. A specific everyday context (car mirror) is the only setting that felt fresh. Naira's pool already has hand-in-context heroes (H03, H07, H13, H14) and a consistent on-model worn set for grids.

Layout waste: the 9:16 canvases cram content into the top 55-65% and leave the lower third empty, or put offer strips where the Story reply bar sits. There are on-image SHOP NOW buttons that duplicate Meta's button, plus tiny T&C text and a broken apostrophe glyph. Naira should fill the y=270-1500 band, skip or shrink the on-image CTA, and check glyphs at phone size.

Every jewellery ad in the batch leads with a discount or code (GIVA 15% NEW15, GIVA 20% BLING, Palmonas 50% twice), and the codes come with T&C clutter. The category is saturated with percent-off hooks. Naira should differentiate with the price floor ('from ₹599') and put 'Buy 3, 20% off, applied in your bag' low in the hierarchy or as the twist, never as a code.

The only ad that shows an actual price (Snitch ₹1599) is the clearest and most honest offer here. No jeweller shows a rupee price on the image, so a big, true price on a whole-collection ad is open ground.

The lines are generic everywhere: 'Own Your Look', 'Crafted Boldly', 'Gifts that feel personal', 'When in doubt, GIFT GIVA.' None names a real thing. Naira's 'named Indian thing, turned' lines (anaar, rangoli, pheni) are the moat. Don't trade them for slogans.

No competitor ad here sells breadth. Each shows one product or one gift combo. A Shop All that visibly shows many pieces, on her, has the territory to itself, and Naira's own data says worn-photo catalogue carousels convert best (5.45% / 33 purchases; 4.37% / 41 purchases).

Gifting is the default jewellery frame (GIVA chat, both Palmonas), usually a partner buying for 'her'. Naira's buyer shops for herself and the women around her, so 'Didi, Mummy and me' with the multi-buy is a sharper version of the same moment. Tie it to no deadline, since delivery is 3-5 working days.

Contrast decides the stop. The strongest frames have a dark or saturated value somewhere (Palmonas emerald on chocolate, Lenskart amber on black, Snitch giant tonal type). The weakest are pastel on pastel (Palmonas blush) or silver-tone on grey (GIVA split). Naira's pool is mostly cream, so give some concepts a deep ground (H15 maroon saree, H13 or H07 dark bokeh) or an amber-to-black backdrop behind cut-outs.

9:16 creatives often waste their lower 20-30% (GIVA split, GIVA chat, Palmonas brown), and GIVA's chat floats in the middle half at about 20 px type. Design Feed and Story separately: fill y=270-1500 on Story, 4:5 with 60 px margins on Feed, and keep body type at 30 px or more.

The 'idea' ads are the native or lo-fi ones (GIVA chat bubbles, the Lenskart selfie-plus-ticket), and the polished ones are templates (Lenskart's series, Palmonas' box-on-ground). The best Shop All combines both: a repeatable card template (same type position, one piece per card, ground colour sampled from the stone) with one native-format opener that earns the stop.

Product on packaging (both Palmonas ads, GIVA chat) signals 'gift-ready' without words. The pool has no Naira box photo, so use the true line 'Every piece arrives in the Naira gift box.' and the H09 potli scene. Don't stage a box.

Product naming works: Lenskart names 'Vincent Chase Sleek Steel', Snitch names the price. Specific beats adjectives, so every Naira card should carry the piece name and exact price (₹1,199, with the Indian comma).

Rule-breakers to avoid copying: multi-line ALL CAPS (Snitch, 'GIFT GIVA.'), '% OFF' as the biggest type, codes and T&C on the image, newness or urgency claims ('Just stepped in stock'), and CGI-looking levitation, which for jewellery reads as a render.
